angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 549,603 km at 102.44 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 9.7621 +/- 0.0215 mas (same row, RUWE 1.03): 102.44 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.79 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-229 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract): 549,603 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.87 +/- 0.01 solar masses from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-229 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5315 +/- 35 K from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-229 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-229 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-229.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.582, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
